## 4. Analyse de sensibilité stochastique

### Simulation stochastique de MC

\
Distribution des marges brutes et écart entre scénario (référence, mhe) suivant des jeux de données tirés aléatoirement, dans des distributions normales bornées, de valeurs des paramètres d'élevage (taux d'abattage, mortalité vache et veau, IVV) et des prix de vente (vache et broutard mâles et femelles). Résultats :

\
nb : l'adoption de min et max dès le fichier yaml de valeurs de distribution des paramètres limite les warnings dus à des tirages aboutissant à un taux de réforme mhe négatif tronqué à 0 et les warnings dus à des tirages aboutissant à un nbre de génisses vendues négatif tronqué à 0. Reste \<5% de warnings

```{r}
#| label: stochastic
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1) Charger les paramètres de distributions ---
dist_tbl <- read.csv(here::here("config/stochastic_2023.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# --- 2) Sampler-----
rnorm_clamp <- function(mean, sd, minv = -Inf, maxv = Inf) {
  x <- rnorm(1, mean, sd)
  x <- max(min(x, maxv), minv)
  x
}

# bornes par défaut
param_bounds <- function(name) {
  switch(name,
    "CU_RA"    = c(0, 1),
    "MO_RA_AF" = c(0, 1),
    "MO_RA_Y"  = c(0, 1),
    "IVV"      = c(250, 520),     #  pour éviter valeurs absurdes
    # prix et coûts : bornes larges
    "LA_VAL_AF"= c(0, Inf),
    "LA_VAL_JM"= c(0, Inf),
   "LA_VAL_JF"= c(0, Inf),
    c(-Inf, Inf)
  )
}

draw_params_once <- function(base_params, dist_tbl) {
  p <- base_params
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(dist_tbl))) {
    nm   <- dist_tbl$param[i]
    dist <- dist_tbl$dist[i]
    mu   <- dist_tbl$mean[i]
    sd   <- dist_tbl$sd[i]
    rng  <- param_bounds(nm)

    val <- switch(dist,
      "normal" = rnorm_clamp(mu, sd, rng[1], rng[2]),
      stop(sprintf("Distribution '%s' non gérée pour %s", dist, nm))
    )

    p[[nm]] <- val
  }
  p
}

# --- 3) Monte Carlo autour de la référence ---
run_mc <- function(B = 1000, seed = 123) {
  set.seed(seed)
  out <- vector("list", B)

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    # 3.1 Tirer un jeu de paramètres
    p_ref <- draw_params_once(params, dist_tbl)

    # 3.2 calcul du TR_eff_ref = CU_RA + MO_RA_AF du TIRAGE*
    TR_eff_ref_row <- p_ref$CU_RA + p_ref$MO_RA_AF

    # 3.3 Scénario REF
    res_ref <- run_scenario(p_ref, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = FALSE)

    # 3.4 Scénario MHE (impacts constants ; TR_eff_ref_row inchangé)*
    p_mhe <- apply_impacts(p_ref, impacts_mhe)
    p_mhe$COST_VET_D <- 15
    p_mhe$SH_PCR     <- 0
    p_mhe$C_PCR      <- 25
    res_mhe <- run_scenario(p_mhe, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = TRUE)

    out[[b]] <- data.frame(
      draw = b,
      MB_ref = res_ref$MB_op,
      MB_mhe = res_mhe$MB_op,
      dMB    = res_mhe$MB_op - res_ref$MB_op
    )
  }

  do.call(rbind, out)
}

# --- 4) Lancer, résumer, visualiser ---
mc_res <- run_mc(B = 2000, seed = 42)

# Résumé statistique
summ <- within(data.frame(
  mean_MB_ref = mean(mc_res$MB_ref),
  sd_MB_ref   = sd(mc_res$MB_ref),
  mean_MB_mhe = mean(mc_res$MB_mhe),
  sd_MB_mhe   = sd(mc_res$MB_mhe),
  mean_dMB    = mean(mc_res$dMB),
  sd_dMB      = sd(mc_res$dMB),
  q05_dMB     = quantile(mc_res$dMB, 0.05),
  q50_dMB     = quantile(mc_res$dMB, 0.50),
  q95_dMB     = quantile(mc_res$dMB, 0.95),
  p_dMB_neg   = mean(mc_res$dMB < 0)
), {})


kable(summ)


#| label: sim_interval_normal
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)
library(knitr)



```

### Stochastic simulation with breakdown

```{r}
#| label: stochastic_decompos
#| warning: false


# --- 1) Charger les paramètres de distributions ---
dist_tbl <- read.csv(here::here("config/stochastic_2023.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# --- 2) Sampler-----
rnorm_clamp <- function(mean, sd, minv = -Inf, maxv = Inf) {
  x <- rnorm(1, mean, sd)
  x <- max(min(x, maxv), minv)
  x
}

# bornes par défaut
param_bounds <- function(name) {
  switch(name,
    "CU_RA"    = c(0, 1),
    "MO_RA_AF" = c(0, 1),
    "MO_RA_Y"  = c(0, 1),
    "IVV"      = c(250, 520),     #  pour éviter valeurs absurdes
    # prix et coûts : bornes larges
    "LA_VAL_AF"= c(0, Inf),
    "LA_VAL_JM"= c(0, Inf),
   "LA_VAL_JF"= c(0, Inf),
    c(-Inf, Inf)
  )
}

draw_params_once <- function(base_params, dist_tbl) {
  p <- base_params
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(dist_tbl))) {
    nm   <- dist_tbl$param[i]
    dist <- dist_tbl$dist[i]
    mu   <- dist_tbl$mean[i]
    sd   <- dist_tbl$sd[i]
    rng  <- param_bounds(nm)

    val <- switch(dist,
      "normal" = rnorm_clamp(mu, sd, rng[1], rng[2]),
      stop(sprintf("Distribution '%s' non gérée pour %s", dist, nm))
    )

    p[[nm]] <- val
  }
  p
}


# --- Helper : récupérer REV_Y total même si m/f sont séparés ---
get_REV_Y <- function(bd) {
  if (!is.null(bd$REV_Y)) {
    bd$REV_Y
  } else if (!is.null(bd$REV_Y_m) && !is.null(bd$REV_Y_f)) {
    bd$REV_Y_m + bd$REV_Y_f
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
}

# --- Monte Carlo avec décomposition complète (REF & MHE) ---
run_mc_decomp <- function(B = 2000, seed = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  out <- vector("list", B)

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    # 1) Tirage de paramètres autour de la référence
    p_ref <- draw_params_once(params, dist_tbl)

    # 2) TR_eff_ref du tirage (règle v03)
    TR_eff_ref_row <- p_ref$CU_RA + p_ref$MO_RA_AF

    # 3) Scénario REF
    res_ref <- run_scenario(p_ref, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = FALSE)

    # 4) Scénario MHE : impacts constants (tes 'impacts_mhe') + surcoûts
    p_mhe <- apply_impacts(p_ref, impacts_mhe)
    p_mhe$COST_VET_D <- 15
    p_mhe$SH_PCR     <- 0
    p_mhe$C_PCR      <- 25
    res_mhe <- run_scenario(p_mhe, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = TRUE)

    # 5) Empiler la décomposition pour REF et MHE
    out[[b]] <- rbind(
      data.frame(
        draw = b, scen = "REF",
        REV_AF     = res_ref$breakdown$REV_AF,
        REV_Y      = get_REV_Y(res_ref$breakdown),
        COST_PROD  = res_ref$breakdown$COST_PROD,
        COST_VET_D = res_ref$breakdown$COST_VET_D,
        COST_RESTR = res_ref$breakdown$COST_RESTR,
        MB_op      = res_ref$MB_op,
        check.names = FALSE
      ),
      data.frame(
        draw = b, scen = "MHE",
        REV_AF     = res_mhe$breakdown$REV_AF,
        REV_Y      = get_REV_Y(res_mhe$breakdown),
        COST_PROD  = res_mhe$breakdown$COST_PROD,
        COST_VET_D = res_mhe$breakdown$COST_VET_D,
        COST_RESTR = res_mhe$breakdown$COST_RESTR,
        MB_op      = res_mhe$MB_op,
        check.names = FALSE
      )
    )
  }

  dplyr::bind_rows(out)
}

# --- Lancer et calculer les MOYENNES par scénario ---
mc_decomp <- run_mc_decomp(B = 2000, seed = 42)

moyennes_stoch <- mc_decomp %>%
  dplyr::group_by(scen) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    REV_AF     = mean(REV_AF,     na.rm = TRUE),
    REV_Y      = mean(REV_Y,      na.rm = TRUE),
    COST_PROD  = mean(COST_PROD,  na.rm = TRUE),
    COST_VET_D = mean(COST_VET_D, na.rm = TRUE),
    COST_RESTR = mean(COST_RESTR, na.rm = TRUE),
    MB_op      = mean(MB_op,      na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

moyennes_stoch

```

### GRAPH stochastic model

```{r}
#| label: graph_stoch_en
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# Expected structure of `moyennes_stoch`:
#   scen ∈ { "REF","EHD" }, and columns:
#   REV_AF, REV_Y, COST_PROD, COST_VET_D, COST_RESTR, MB_op

# 1) Long format + sign conventions (costs displayed as negative)
sd_all <- moyennes_stoch %>%
 mutate(scenario = recode(scen, "REF" = "EHD-free", "MHE" = "EHD")) %>%
  select(scenario, REV_AF, REV_Y, COST_PROD, COST_VET_D, COST_RESTR, MB_op) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -scenario,
    names_to = "step",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    value = case_when(
      step %in% c("COST_PROD", "COST_VET_D", "COST_RESTR") ~ -value,
      TRUE ~ value
    ),
    type = case_when(
      step %in% c("REV_AF","REV_Y") ~ "PRODUCTS (sales)",
      step %in% c("COST_PROD","COST_VET_D","COST_RESTR") ~ "COSTS",
      step %in% c("MB_op") ~ "MARGIN"
    )
  )

# 2) Order and labels
step_levels <- c("COST_VET_D", "REV_AF", "REV_Y", "COST_PROD", "MB_op")
step_labels <- c(
  COST_VET_D = "Veterinary (EHD)",
  REV_AF     = "Culled cows",
  REV_Y      = "Weanlings",
  COST_PROD  = "Production",
  MB_op      = "Operating margin"
)

sd_all$type <- factor(sd_all$type, levels = c("COSTS", "PRODUCTS (sales)", "MARGIN"))
sd_all$scenario <- factor(sd_all$scenario, levels = c("EHD-free", "EHD"))

# Optionally drop COST_RESTR
if (all(sd_all$step != "COST_RESTR" | sd_all$value == 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  sd_all <- subset(sd_all, step != "COST_RESTR")
}

# 3) Plot
ggplot(sd_all,
       aes(x = factor(step, levels = step_levels, labels = step_labels),
           y = value, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6) +

  # English-style euro formatting
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = paste0("€", format(round(value, 0), big.mark = ",", decimal.mark = ".")),
      vjust = ifelse(value >= 0, -0.4, 1.3)
    ),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
    size = 3.2, color = "black"
  ) +

  facet_grid(. ~ type, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", switch = "x") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, color = "grey30") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(
      accuracy = 1,
      big.mark = ",",
      decimal.mark = ".",
      prefix = "€"
    ),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.15))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Stochastic decomposition (means) – EHD-free vs EHD",
    x = NULL, y = "€/cow", fill = NULL
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("EHD-free" = "grey6", "EHD" = "#722222")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.placement = "outside"
  )


```

### Gross Margin Distribution and dGM ( probability density)

#### Distribution de la MB (courbe de densité) dans le modèle stochastique

Pour rendre compte de la dissymétrie, on utilise non pas la moyenne+ sd mais médiane+IQ

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

MB_REF_DET <- 552
q_ref <- quantile(mc_res$MB_ref, c(.25, .5, .75), na.rm = TRUE)
q1r <- q_ref[1]; q2r <- q_ref[2]; q3r <- q_ref[3]

p_ref <- ggplot(mc_res, aes(x = MB_ref)) +
  # bande IQR (Q1-Q3)
  annotate("rect", xmin = q1r, xmax = q3r, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           alpha = 0.10, fill = "grey50") +
#  geom_histogram(bins = 40, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_density(linewidth = 1) +
  # lignes verticales
  geom_vline(xintercept = q2r,        colour = "#d95f02", linetype = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = q1r,        colour = "#7570b3", linetype = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = q3r,        colour = "#7570b3", linetype = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of gross margin – stochastic model",
    subtitle = sprintf("Median: %.0f  |  IQR: [%.0f – %.0f]",
                       q2r, q1r, q3r),
    x = "Gross margin of the EHD-free scenario (€/cow/year)", y = "Probability density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_ref
```

## 5. Analyse de sensibilité des paramètres MHE

### Analyse déterministe (diagramme Tornado)

Le scenario de base est celui de 2023 et les bornes choisies sont :mortalité adulte : de 0 à 8% ; mortalité veau - 6 mois : de 0 à 20 % ; IVV : de 355 à 430 jours. Rappel taux d'abattage n'intervient pas.

```{r}
#| label: tornado
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# --- cible : dMB ---
target_fun <- function(res_ref, res_mhe) res_mhe$MB_op - res_ref$MB_op

# --- règle v03 : TR_eff_ref calculé sur la ref, réutilisé en MHE ---
TR_eff_ref_row <- params$CU_RA + params$MO_RA_AF

res_ref0 <- run_scenario(params, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = FALSE)

apply_mhe_and_run <- function(p_ref, impacts) {
  # mapping éventuel du nom 'dMO_RA' -> 'dCU_RA'
  if (!is.null(impacts$dMO_RA) && is.null(impacts$dCU_RA)) {
    impacts$dCU_RA <- impacts$dMO_RA
  }
  p_mhe <- apply_impacts(p_ref, impacts)

  # cap mortalité adulte en MHE pour éviter CU_RA_used < 0
  if (p_mhe$MO_RA_AF > TR_eff_ref_row) p_mhe$MO_RA_AF <- TR_eff_ref_row

  # surcoûts (si besoin)
  p_mhe$COST_VET_D <- 15
  p_mhe$SH_PCR     <- 0
  p_mhe$C_PCR      <- 25

  run_scenario(p_mhe, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = TRUE)
}

# --- impacts "centraux" (s'assurer qu'ils existent) ---
# ex. si déjà définis : impacts_mhe_base <- list(dMO_RA_AF=0.015, dMO_RA_Y=0.02, dIVV=21, dCU_RA=0.00)
impacts_mhe_base <- impacts_mhe
res_mhe0    <- apply_mhe_and_run(params, impacts_mhe)
base_target <- target_fun(res_ref0, res_mhe0)

# --- bornes ONE-WAY fournies — SANS dCU_RA (non utilisé dans le calcul de MB) ---
bounds <- list(
  dMO_RA_AF = c(low = -0.03,  high =  0.05),
  dMO_RA_Y  = c(low = -0.08,  high =  0.12),
  dIVV      = c(low = -30,    high =  45)
)


# --- one-way tornado : on varie 1 impact, les autres = valeur centrale ---
run_oneway <- function(impact_name, low_val, high_val) {
  imp_low  <- impacts_mhe_base
  imp_high <- impacts_mhe_base
  imp_low[[impact_name]]  <- low_val
  imp_high[[impact_name]] <- high_val

  res_mhe_low  <- apply_mhe_and_run(params, imp_low)
  res_mhe_high <- apply_mhe_and_run(params, imp_high)

  tibble::tibble(
    impact = impact_name,
    low    = target_fun(res_ref0, res_mhe_low),
    high   = target_fun(res_ref0, res_mhe_high)
  )
}

torn_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(bounds), function(nm) {
  run_oneway(nm, bounds[[nm]]["low"], bounds[[nm]]["high"])
})) %>%
  mutate(min_val = pmin(low, high),
         max_val = pmax(low, high),
         base    = base_target,
         from    = min_val - base,
         to      = max_val - base) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(to - from)))

#dictionnaire
labels_map <- c(
  dMO_RA_AF = "cow mortality rate",
  dMO_RA_Y  = "calf mortality rate",
  dIVV      = "calving interval"
)


torn_df$impact_label <- labels_map[torn_df$impact]


# --- graphique tornado ---
ggplot(torn_df, aes(y = reorder(impact_label, abs(to - from)))) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = from, xend = to, yend = impact_label), linewidth = 6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Tornado – influence of EHD impacts on ΔGM",
    subtitle = "One-way sensitivity with expert-defined bounds",
    x = "Variation of ΔGM around baseline (€/cow/year)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()



```

### Analyse stochastique, en utilisant des valeurs d'impact aux bornes de leur IC

Sauf pour IVV, les effets ont été évalués sur 6 mois donc divisés par 2 (hypothèse : pas d'effet dûs à la MHE le restant de l'année)

```{r}
#| label: dMB_stocha
#| echo: false
# --- IC de ΔMB via MC sur les IMPACTS (dMO_RA_AF, dMO_RA_Y, dIVV) ---

library(dplyr)

## 0) Réglages (réf. et z pour IC95 %)
base_mo_ra_af <- 0.03   # 3 %/an
base_mo_ra_y  <- 0.096  # 9.6 %/an
z <- qnorm(0.975)

## 1) Paramétrisation des distributions d'impacts

# Adultes (IRR 1.65, IC 0.85–3.21) -> on échantillonne sur l'échelle log (log-normal)
irr_af_hat <- 1.65; irr_af_lo <- 0.85; irr_af_hi <- 3.21
sdlog_af   <- (log(irr_af_hi) - log(irr_af_lo)) / (2*z)
meanlog_af <- log(irr_af_hat)

# Veaux (IRR 1.41, IC 1.03–1.95) -> pareil
irr_y_hat <- 1.41; irr_y_lo <- 1.03; irr_y_hi <- 1.95
sdlog_y   <- (log(irr_y_hi) - log(irr_y_lo)) / (2*z)
meanlog_y <- log(irr_y_hat)

# IVV (effet annuel) : β = 11.3 jours, IC [6.7 ; 15.9]
ivv_mu <- 11.3
ivv_sd <- (15.9 - 6.7) / (2*z)

## 2) Sampler d'impacts (N tirages)
sample_impacts <- function(N = 2000, seed = 123) {
  set.seed(seed)
  irr_af <- rlnorm(N, meanlog_af, sdlog_af)
  irr_y  <- rlnorm(N, meanlog_y,  sdlog_y)
  dIVV   <- rnorm(N, ivv_mu, ivv_sd)           # jours, effet annuel

  # Rappel : mortalités sur 6 mois -> demi-effet (pondération 0.5)
  dMO_RA_AF <- base_mo_ra_af * 0.5 * (irr_af - 1)
  dMO_RA_Y  <- base_mo_ra_y  * 0.5 * (irr_y  - 1)

  tibble::tibble(dMO_RA_AF = dMO_RA_AF, dMO_RA_Y = dMO_RA_Y, dIVV = dIVV)
}

## 3) Monte Carlo ΔMB (impacts uniquement)
mc_dmb_from_impacts <- function(B = 2000, seed = 123) {
  draws <- sample_impacts(B, seed)

  # TR_eff_ref calculé sur la référence (règle v03)
  TR_eff_ref_row <- params$CU_RA + params$MO_RA_AF
  res_ref0 <- run_scenario(params, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = FALSE)

  out <- vector("numeric", B)

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    imp <- list(
      dMO_RA_AF = draws$dMO_RA_AF[b],
      dMO_RA_Y  = draws$dMO_RA_Y[b],
      dIVV      = draws$dIVV[b],
      dCU_RA    = 0.0         # n'intervient pas dans ton moteur courant
    )

    p_mhe <- apply_impacts(params, imp)

    # garde-fous usuels
    if (p_mhe$MO_RA_AF > TR_eff_ref_row) p_mhe$MO_RA_AF <- TR_eff_ref_row
    p_mhe$COST_VET_D <- 15; p_mhe$SH_PCR <- 0; p_mhe$C_PCR <- 25

    res_mhe <- run_scenario(p_mhe, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = TRUE)
    out[b]  <- res_mhe$MB_op - res_ref0$MB_op   # ΔMB
  }

  out
}

## 4) Lancer et résumer
dMB_mc <- mc_dmb_from_impacts(B = 5000, seed = 42)

ic <- quantile(dMB_mc, c(.025, .5, .975), na.rm = TRUE)
mean_dMB <- mean(dMB_mc, na.rm = TRUE); sd_dMB <- sd(dMB_mc, na.rm = TRUE)

data.frame(
  cible = "ΔMB = MB(MHE) - MB(Ref)",
  mean  = round(mean_dMB, 1),
  median= round(ic[2], 1),
  q2.5  = round(ic[1], 1),
  q97.5 = round(ic[3], 1),
  sd    = round(sd_dMB, 1)
)
```
